page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a mixture of average single-core capabilities and weaker multi-core scaling. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance and gzip compression are in the average tier, while multi-core stress-ng and bzip3 decompression fall into the weak and poor categories respectively. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large block read and write speeds categorized as weak. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in cryptographic execution, static web serving throughput at 6.28 GB/sec, and small-model LLM inference, achieving 107.71 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M model.

Given its hardware profile, the ecs.c7.xlarge offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-bound workloads that do not require high memory density or local storage. The primary tradeoff is the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and weak multi-threaded scaling, which makes it less suitable for large databases or memory-intensive applications. It is best suited for single-threaded processing, lightweight web serving, basic cryptographic tasks, and small-scale machine learning inference.
